newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at 7-year peak on electronics.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at 7-year peak on electronics.

text.p: Taiwan share prices, riding on momentum from bellwether electronic stocks, ended at another seven-year high on Monday.
But brokers warned the recent bull run may have hit a snag after the index failed to crack the 9,600-point resistance.
The benchmark stock index had soared to an intra-day high of 9626.34, but lost steam in late trade and finished 92.46 points or 0.97 percent higher at 9,593.54.
Despite failing to stand above 9,600, the close still surpassed the 9,501.08 finish on Saturday and was the index's highest level since it closed at 9,665.50 on April 28, 1990.
Turnover was a hectic T$210 billion.
Brokers said electronics, which rose 4.71 percent to lead Monday's rally, had defied expected profit-taking to carry the overall index while other sectors slipped from recent peaks.
"The electronics industry is expected to do better in the second half of this year, based on its revenue gains in the first half," said Jeffrey Liang, analyst for Nomura Securities.
Motherboard maker Asustek soared by the daily seven-percent limit or T$28 to T$433. Chipmaker Winbond also hit limit-up, gaining T$4.5 to T$69.5.
Microchip maker United Micro surged T$10 to T$154. Compact disc maker Ritek Incorp finished limit-up to T$246.

Recently rejuvenating construction shares, which opened higher on a surprisingly high weekend land auction bid by a China Development Corp consortium, turned sharply lower after failing to find fundamental support, brokers said.
